templates_considered: no_destructive_sql (SEC-010): forbids raw SQL and truncation, not ordinary db.del; the ask is about deletes, so it only partly fits and was not used
writes_check_first (BIZ-001): stack.statement_order for checks before writes; does not cover delete or approval, so did not fit
endpoints_need_login, admin_endpoints_check_role, protected_endpoints_run_middleware: about endpoint auth and roles, not agent tools; did not fit
no_leftover_code, tables_have_listed_fields, others: unrelated to the ask; did not fit

rules.covers: agents can't delete anything (tool stacks, including functions they call)
agents can't email customers without a human approving first

ask_parts_not_covered.part: agents shouldn't call tools the user hasn't explicitly given them
human approval is actually enforced at runtime, not just present in the stored definition
delete via bulk writes (db.bulk.*) and delete-like calls to external services (api.request DELETE)
ask_parts_not_covered.why: other: not in the ask's exact wording; I left them out rather than guessing a wider scope

assumptions: Agent tools are the only objects an AI agent runs; the endpoints and the delete_user_account function are reachable only if a tool calls them, and stack.statement_forbidden follows function calls
util.send_email is the statement name for sending email; db.del and db.truncate are the delete statement names
request_human_approval is the approval gate, as used by issue_refund
tags = ["ai-agents"] on the policies is a tag I made up; the workspace has no tag vocabulary I could find
confusions: object.statement_required: the description says 'Set statements or functions; with both, the statement must call one of the functions', but the 'when' param says 'statement' is a single name; unclear whether 'when.statement' can be a list
No check reads an agent's tool list, though the catalogue includes 'agent' in object_kinds for several checks; not clear which check, if any, can see agent.tools

stack.statement_forbidden says tools are judged as their own object, and functions they call are followed; it is not stated whether db.del reached through function.run is reported at the tool or at the function, which matters for the finding location
Whether a policy with no tags needs a tag at all; the policy file format shows tags as optional but the examples always have them
wished_for: A check that reads an agent's tool list (for example agent.tools against an allowlist)
A worked example of object.statement_required with when.statement for an approval gate, showing placement unconditional vs first
A list of statement names (db.del, util.send_email, etc.) so I can confirm each name without guessing
why_confidence: Both rules parse cleanly and match the delete and email parts of the ask, but I have not run xano policy evaluate, so the findings I expect are predictions. The tool-allowlist part has no check, and the approval gate is only checked in the stored definition, not at runtime.
